\[
\begin{gathered}
A = G_{\sigma} * \begin{pmatrix} I_x^2 & I_x I_y \\ I_x I_y & I_y^2 \end{pmatrix},\qquad R = \lambda_{\min}(A) = \tfrac{1}{2}\left(\operatorname{tr} A - \sqrt{(A_{xx} - A_{yy})^2 + 4 A_{xy}^2}\right)
\end{gathered}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(A\): The structure tensor
- \(I_x, I_y\): The Sobel derivatives
- \(G_{\sigma}\): The Gaussian window

I_x and I_y are the Sobel derivatives of the image on a 0 to 1 scale. G_sigma * blurs each entry of the matrix with a Gaussian, so A sums the gradients around each pixel. A has two large eigenvalues at a corner, one at an edge and none in a flat area. Shi and Tomasi used the smaller eigenvalue, which is large only when the brightness changes in every direction. The corners output marks pixels whose response is at least the threshold and at least every response within the minimum distance. Plateaus keep every pixel. This is the rule of the filter, and it differs from skimage.feature.corner_peaks, which also drops corners near the border.
